title: Pitch & Frequency
description: High notes and low notes — what's the difference? Master pitch to tune fragment 6 into the Harmony Bell.

content.value: PITCH is how high or low a sound seems. It depends on FREQUENCY — how fast the object vibrates. A fast vibration (high frequency) gives a HIGH pitch; a slow vibration (low frequency) gives a LOW pitch.

HIGH frequency → HIGH pitch  🎵  (whistle, bird, mosquito)
LOW frequency  → LOW pitch    🎶  (drum, roar, big bell)

A tiny mosquito's fast wing-beats give a high whine. A big drum's slow vibration gives a deep, low boom. A child's voice is higher-pitched than an adult's because their short vocal cords vibrate faster.
Loudness vs Pitch — Don't Mix Them Up!

LOUDNESS ← AMPLITUDE (how big the vibration is)
PITCH    ← FREQUENCY (how fast it vibrates)

A quiet high note and a loud high note have the SAME pitch
but different loudness. They are separate ideas!
Two words to keep straight: bigger amplitude = LOUDER (not higher). Faster frequency = HIGHER pitch (not louder). Amplitude → loudness, frequency → pitch.
Key Takeaway: Pitch depends on frequency — faster vibration gives a higher pitch. Loudness (from amplitude) and pitch (from frequency) are two completely separate properties of a sound.

quiz.question: The pitch of a sound depends on its…
quiz.explain: Higher frequency (faster vibration) gives a higher pitch.

quiz.question: A mosquito's high whine compared to a drum's low boom has a…
quiz.explain: The high pitch comes from the mosquito's fast wing vibration — a higher frequency.

quiz.explain: Loudness is set by amplitude; pitch is set by frequency. They are separate properties.
